request.spec:
A quick-add bar on the people list takes a name and an amount and creates a DRAFT claim with that
amount, dated the sheet's today, with an empty note, for the named person. If the name is not on
the sheet the person is created first with grade A. Every rule that applies to the person and
claim forms applies here, and a refusal shows an error on the bar. The whole quick-add is one
change: a refused claim leaves no new person behind and writes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A quick-add bar on the people list takes a name and an amount and creates a DRAFT claim with that
amount, dated the sheet's today, with an empty note, for the named person. If the name is not on
the sheet the person is created first with grade A. Every rule that applies to the person and
claim forms applies here, and a refusal shows an error on the bar. The whole quick-add is one
change: a refused claim leaves no new person behind and writes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The quick-add bar is in place, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests: the quick-add test and the three existing scenarios.

**Server:** there's a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/quick-add`, defined in `quick-add.POST.yml`. Its new step classes are in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/quickadd/`.
- **Checks first, saves second.** An empty name is refused with the person-form error. An amount the claim form would refuse is refused with the claim-form error. A claim whose date (the sheet's today) falls in a closed period is also refused. All of these checks happen before anything is stored. The app writes audit lines straight to the file, so this ordering is what makes a refusal leave no new person behind and write no audit lines.
- **Finding or adding the person.** The name is trimmed and matched ignoring case, so " dot " finds Dot, the same way the person form treats names as duplicates. If no one matches, the person is created with grade A, and the same `PERSON_ADDED` and `ROLLUP` lines are written as when adding a person through the person form.
- **Adding the claim.** This reuses the existing claim steps (`BuildClaim`, `AuditClaimAdded`, `AuditRollup`, `RespondWithClaim`). The claim is a DRAFT with the sheet's today as its date and an empty note. Once a new person is added, the figures are noted again, so the claim's own `ROLLUP` line only reports what the claim itself changed.

**Front end:** the bar is `src/main/frontend/features/people/quickadd.slot.tsx`, and it sits just above the people list. It has `quick-name`, `quick-amount`, `quick-submit` and `quick-error`. The error clears as soon as you edit a field or submit again. After a successful add, it reloads the people and claims and empties both fields.

The closed-period refusal isn't covered by the test, so that path hasn't been run.
